chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi', from Muhammad ibn Zayd who said:
I came to al-Rida (peace be upon him) to ask him about tawhid. So he dictated to me:

'Praise be to Allah, Originator of things by their bringing into existence and their Initiator — by His power and His wisdom — not from anything, so that creation would be invalidated, nor for a cause, so that initiation would not be sound. He created what He willed, however He willed, uniquely so, to manifest His wisdom and the reality of His Lordship. Intellects cannot comprehend Him, imaginations cannot reach Him, sights cannot perceive Him, no measure can encompass Him. Expression falls short before Him, sights are dulled before Him, and the applications of attributes go astray in Him. He is veiled without a veil that veils, hidden without a covering that conceals, known without being seen, described without form, and characterized without body. There is no god but Allah, the Great, the Most High.'

key_terms.الابتداع: Al-ibtida': initiation, primordial innovation; creation without a prior efficient cause
key_terms.الاختراع: Al-ikhtirar: invention/creation ex nihilo; used to argue God did not create from pre-existing matter
key_terms.التوحيد: Tawhid: Divine Unity/Oneness — the central Islamic theological doctrine
key_terms.الربوبية: Al-rububiyya: Lordship, the quality of being the Master and Sustainer of all things
key_terms.تصاريف الصفات: Tasarif al-sifat: the 'applications of attributes' — normal predication fails when applied to God
key_terms.فاطر: Fatir: Originator, One who creates from nothing without precedent

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Rida say about the nature of Allah and Divine Unity (tawhid)?
ai.summary: In this profound theological statement, Imam Ali al-Rida (AS) dictated to Muhammad ibn Zayd a concise creed on Divine Unity (tawhid). The Imam articulates God's absolute transcendence: He created all things from nothing, not from pre-existing matter (which would negate invention) and not for any prior cause (which would compromise the spontaneity of initiation). God's creation is entirely free and sovereign. The Imam then employs a series of paradoxes characteristic of apophatic theology: God is beyond the grasp of intellects, imagination, and sight; He is veiled yet not by any material veil; He is known without visual perception; He is described without physical form. The statement concludes with the shahada formula affirming Divine transcendence. This hadith was taught in the context of 3rd-century theological debates, when rationalist Mu'tazila and anthropomorphist Mujassima groups were actively contending over God's nature, and the Imam's compact formulation offered a Shia theological anchor.
word_analysis: so that creation would be invalidated

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Al Hassan, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Muhammad Bin Zayd who said,
‘I went over to Al-Rezaasws asking himasws about the Tawheed (Oneness). So heasws dictated unto me:
‘The Praise is for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Originator of the things, their Maker and their Initiator. He<sup>azwj</sup> Initiated these by His<sup>azwj</sup> Power and His<sup>azwj</sup> Wisdom.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn al-Hassan has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘ from Muhammad ibn Zayd who has said the following.
“I went to Imam al-Rida (a.s.) to ask about the Oneness of Allah (God). The Imam dictated to me thus,

‘All praise belongs to Allah, Who is the originator of all things. He is the inventor of all things, an invention that came from His power and wisdom but not from a thing so it would invalidate the invention and not from a cause so it would invalidate the novelty. He created whatever He wanted and howsoever He liked. He alone did all this to manifest His Wisdom and the truth of His Providence. Intelligence cannot comprehend Him, (Awham) imagination cannot reach Him, eyes cannot see Him and measurements cannot confine Him. The power of expression is unable to express Him in words. All sights are exhausted from reaching Him and the power of describing and defining have gone astray in its description and definition of His-self. He is hidden without any veil and is concealed without any covering. He is known without being seen; described without any form, and praised without any body. There is no god, except Allah, the Great, the Most High.’”
